record.paper_title: PROGRESS IN THE OPEN PROBLEMS IN THEORY OF FUNCTIONS OF BOUNDED INDEX
record.context_brief: Max-min criterion for bounded directional index
record.original_question: Let L belong to the class Q_b^n of positive continuous functions for which the regularity quantity λ_b(η) is finite for every η > 0. Is the following criterion equivalent to bounded L-index in the direction b for an entire function F on C^n: there exist constants R > 0, P_2(R) ≥ 1, and η(R) ∈ (0,R) such that for every z_0 ∈ C^n one can choose r = r(z_0) in [η(R), R] with max{|F(z_0 + tb)| : |t| = r/L(z_0)} ≤ P_2(R) min{|F(z_0 + tb)| : |t| = r/L(z_0)}?

evidence.quote: By Q^n_b we denote the class of functions L such that λ(η) is finite for any η > 0.

Conjecture 1. Let L ∈ Q^n_b. An entire function F(z) is of bounded L-index in direction b ∈ C^n if and only if there exist R > 0, P2(R) ≥ 1 and η(R) ∈ (0, R) such that for all z0 ∈ C^n and some r = r(z0) ∈ [η(R), R] inequality max{|F(z0 + tb)|: |t| = r/L(z0)} ≤ P2 min{|F(z0 + tb)|: |t| = r/L(z0)} holds.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a direction $b \in \mathbb{C}^n \setminus \{0\}$. For a positive continuous function $L: \mathbb{C}^n \to (0,\infty)$ and $\eta > 0$, define the regularity quantity
$$\lambda_b(\eta) = \sup\!\left\{ \frac{L(z + t_2 b)}{L(z + t_1 b)} : z \in \mathbb{C}^n,\ t_1, t_2 \in \mathbb{C},\ |t_1 - t_2| \le \frac{\eta}{L(z + t_1 b)} \right\},$$
and let $Q_b^n$ denote the class of all such $L$ for which $\lambda_b(\eta) < \infty$ for every $\eta > 0$.

An entire function $F: \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}$ is said to be of bounded $L$-index in the direction $b$ if there exists an integer $m_0 \ge 0$ such that for every $z \in \mathbb{C}^n$ and every nonnegative integer $m$,
$$\frac{|\partial_b^m F(z)|}{m!\, L(z)^m} \le \max_{0 \le k \le m_0} \frac{|\partial_b^k F(z)|}{k!\, L(z)^k},$$
where $\partial_b F(z) = \sum_{j=1}^n b_j \partial F/\partial z_j$.

Let $L \in Q_b^n$ and let $F$ be an entire function on $\mathbb{C}^n$. Prove or disprove: $F$ is of bounded $L$-index in the direction $b$ if and only if there exist constants $R > 0$, $P_2(R) \ge 1$, and $\eta(R) \in (0, R)$ such that for every $z_0 \in \mathbb{C}^n$ there is some $r = r(z_0) \in [\eta(R), R]$ with
$$\max\{|F(z_0 + t b)| : |t| = r/L(z_0)\} \le P_2(R)\, \min\{|F(z_0 + t b)| : |t| = r/L(z_0)\}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (a max-min criterion for bounded $L$-index in a direction for entire functions on $\mathbb{C}^n$) has been proved in the literature on bounded index in direction by Bandura and Skaskiv, and reported as completely proved in subsequent surveys on progress in the theory of functions of bounded index.

status_evidence.title: Progress in open problems in theory of functions of bounded index
status_evidence.claim: The max-min criterion conjecture for bounded L-index in direction has been proved.
